## Stages

Order: Stages 1–3 follow your partner's progression and ranking exactly. Each stage consumes the one before it. Stages 4–7 are the hardening stages that the progression needs later. They come after O3 because none of them is needed for an outcome to work.

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table (core)
      Objective: Ingest every real quarterly and daily master index into one filing-index table at the smallest usable standard.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing. The repository holds empty scaffolds only.
      Produces: a filing-index table covering 1993 Q1 to the latest available daily index, and specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: The table can be queried by CIK, form type and filing date, and it holds rows from every quarterly index and from each daily index of the open quarter. The findings file records the measured cost of the real run: files fetched, bytes, rows, wall time and the observed request rate.
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); replay from retained raw bytes (Stage 4); point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and its findings, including the measured request rate
      Produces: the submissions on disk for the range this stage's spec fixes, with each one locatable from its index row
      Exit: For the chosen range, the downloaded submissions match the index rows that name them, and any gaps are listed by row.
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); replay from retained raw bytes (Stage 4); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings, amendments included, out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: a list of 10-K and 8-K filings, and the extracted main document of each
      Exit: Each 10-K and 8-K in the Stage 2 range, amendments kept distinct, has its main document extracted, or has a listed reason why it was not.
      Leaves out: manifests and provenance (Stage 4); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and provenance; replay from retained raw bytes
      Objective: Give every index row, submission and extracted document a recorded source, and rebuild them from retained bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest that ties each output to its source URL, content hash, receipt time and parser version; retained raw bytes
      Exit: Every output resolves to a manifest entry. Re-running the parse from retained bytes reproduces the same outputs and makes zero SEC requests.
      Leaves out: point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read the quarterly indexes and record the SEC's later additions, changes and withdrawals as versioned generations of the table.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and retained raw bytes
      Produces: versioned filing-index generations, each with a change record
      Exit: A re-read quarter with changed source bytes yields a new generation that lists its additions, changes and withdrawals. The prior generation stays readable.
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover the historical index formats and the failure cases with committed fixtures, run in CI without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: a CI test suite on committed fixtures
      Exit: CI passes offline, with fixtures for each historical index format in the ingested range and for malformed, truncated and HTML-error inputs.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming
      
- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion and reconciliation unattended on a deployed platform.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 4–6 outputs; a platform decision (the background ADR is still only proposed)
      Produces: deployed, scheduled daily ingestion and reconciliation
      Exit: Scheduled runs on two consecutive business days ingest the new daily indexes. Their reports are recorded, and no manual run is involved.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
